q.s: Evidence of seven fire altars in the Harappan civilisation has been found at:
q.x: Kalibangan in Rajasthan yielded the fire altars and a ploughed field; Rangpur is linked with rice husk and the Late Harappan phase.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is NOT located in Haryana?
q.x: Kalibangan is in Rajasthan; Banawali, Rakhigarhi and Bhirrana are in Haryana.

q.s: The Late Harappan 'Cemetery H' culture is associated with which region?
q.x: Cemetery H is the Late Harappan culture of the Harappa region; Rangpur represents the Gujarat phase.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Painted Grey Ware (PGW) is correct?
o: It is a shiny black pottery of the Mauryan age.
It is a coarse red ware of the Chalcolithic Deccan.
It is the characteristic pottery of the Harappan civilisation.
It is grey pottery with linear painted designs, mainly bowls and dishes.
q.x: PGW is the Later Vedic ware; the shiny black ware is the later NBPW.

q.s: The doctrine of Niyati (fate) is associated with which sect?
q.x: Niyati is the Ajivika doctrine of Makkhali Gosala; Anekantavada is Jain and materialism is Charvaka.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a heterodox (non-Vedic) sect of ancient India?
q.x: Nyaya is one of the orthodox (astika) darshanas; Jainism, Ajivika and Charvaka rejected Vedic authority.

q.s: The Jetavana monastery at Sravasti was donated to the Buddha by:
q.x: The merchant Anathapindika bought and donated the Jetavana; Vishakha donated the Pubbarama and Bimbisara the Venuvana.

q.s: Who was the first woman admitted to the Buddhist Sangha as a nun?
q.x: Mahapajapati Gotami, the Buddha's foster mother, was admitted at Vaishali at Ananda's request.

q.s: The Maha Vihara (Parvata Vihara) at Sriparvata was built for Acharya Nagarjuna by the Satavahana king:
q.x: Yajna Sri Satakarni built the great vihara for Nagarjuna at Sriparvata.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Ajivika sect is correct?
o: It survived for only about 500 years.
It finally disappeared from Bengal and Bihar.
It faded with the Puranic-Bhakti revival and the loss of royal patronage.
q.x: Founded by Makkhali Gosala, it lasted about 2,000 years and disappeared from Karnataka and Tamil Nadu in the 14th century.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a Jain centre in early Andhra?
q.x: Munugodu, Kolanupaka and Aryavatam were Jain centres; Nagarjunakonda was a major Buddhist centre.

q.s: The Ashokan edicts were first deciphered in 1837 by:
q.x: James Prinsep deciphered the Brahmi script of the Ashokan edicts in 1837.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a source for the history of the Mauryas?
q.x: The Milindapanho is a dialogue of the Indo-Greek king Menander with Nagasena, of a later period.

q.s: The appointment of Dhamma Mahamatras by Ashoka is recorded in:
q.x: Rock Edict V records the Dhamma Mahamatras (14th regnal year); RE XIII describes the Kalinga war.

q.s: According to Megasthenes, the punishment in the Mauryan state for evading the sales tax was:
o: A fine of double the tax
q.x: Megasthenes records that evasion of the sales tax was punished with death.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Mauryan administration is correct?
o: The Indica was written by Kautilya.
The Mauryas levied no irrigation tax.
Pankodakasannirodhe was the fine for throwing garbage in temples.
According to Megasthenes, evasion of the sales tax was punished with death.
q.x: There was an irrigation tax; Pankodakasannirodhe was the fine for slushing the road; Indica is by Megasthenes.

q.s: The Sanchi stupa is located in which district of Madhya Pradesh?
q.x: Sanchi is in Raisen district, near Vidisha; Bharhut is in Satna district.

q.s: Which of the following stupas is NOT located in Madhya Pradesh?
q.x: Amaravati is in Andhra Pradesh; Sanchi, Bharhut (found by Cunningham) and Satdhara are in MP.

q.s: The Sudarshana lake at Girnar was originally built by Pushyagupta, the governor of:
q.x: Pushyagupta, Chandragupta Maurya's governor, built it; it was later repaired under Rudradaman and under Skandagupta by Parnadatta.

q.s: In the Badami Chalukya administration, the vishaya (district) was headed by the:
q.x: The vishaya was a district under the vishayapati; the Rashtrakutas were feudatories of the Badami Chalukyas.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Badami Chalukyas is correct?
o: The Rashtrakutas were among their feudatories.
They were feudatories of the Pallavas throughout.
Vatapi was a minor village with no trade.
q.x: The Rashtrakutas were their feudatories until Dantidurga overthrew them; Vatapi and Aihole were urban and trade centres.

q.s: The Chola king Rajendra I led a naval expedition in 1025 CE against:
q.x: Rajendra I raided Srivijaya, which controlled the Strait of Malacca and harassed Tamil traders on the China route.

q.s: Balban received the title 'Ulugh Khan' from:
q.x: Nasiruddin Mahmud conferred Ulugh Khan on Balban, whose real name was Baha-ud-din.

q.s: Balban crushed the revolt of Tughril Khan in 1279 in which province?
q.x: Tughril Khan, governor of Bengal, revolted and was crushed by Balban in 1279.

q.s: Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul, a Telugu Brahmin convert from Warangal, served as the Wazir of:
q.x: Khan-i-Jahan Maqbul was Firoz Shah Tughlaq's wazir; Malik Kafur was Alauddin's Naib Malik.

q.s: In the Deccan kingdoms, the foreign Muslims (immigrants from Persia and Central Asia) were known as:
q.x: Foreign Muslims were the Afaqis (Pardesis); the local Deccani Muslims were the Dakhnis.

q.s: Grants of villages to the Bhadrachalam temple were made by which Golconda ruler?
q.x: Abul Hasan Qutb Shah (Tana Shah) made the Bhadrachalam grants.

q.s: In the currency system of Sher Shah Suri, the 'dam' was a coin made of:
q.x: Sher Shah's rupiya was silver (about 178 grains), the dam copper and the mohur gold; one rupiya = 64 dams.

q.s: In the Mughal provinces, the Diwan was made independent of the Subedar in order to:
o: Act as a check on the Subedar
q.x: The provincial Diwan, in charge of revenue and finance, was independent of the Subedar so as to check the governor.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a category in Akbar's classification of land by continuity of cultivation?
q.x: Polaj, Parauti, Chachar and Banjar were the categories; Khalisa was crown land.

q.s: The 'Storia do Mogor', an account of Mughal India, was written by:
q.x: The Venetian Niccolao Manucci wrote the Storia do Mogor; Bernier was physician to Dara Shikoh.

q.s: The French jeweller who traced the Koh-i-Noor diamond to the Kollur mines was:
q.x: Jean-Baptiste Tavernier traced the Koh-i-Noor to Kollur on the Krishna.

q.s: Guru Nanak appointed which of the following as his successor?
q.x: Nanak chose Bhai Lehna, who became Guru Angad in 1539.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT part of Guru Nanak's teachings and practices?
q.x: The Khalsa was founded by Guru Gobind Singh in 1699.

q.s: The title 'Ganj-i-Shakar' is associated with which Sufi saint?
q.x: Baba Farid was Ganj-i-Shakar; Nizamuddin Auliya was Sultan-ul-Mashaikh and Gesudaraz was Banda Nawaz.

q.s: Amir Khusrau was a disciple of which Sufi saint?
q.x: Amir Khusrau was a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya, who was himself a disciple of Baba Farid.

q.s: Which of the following Sufi saints did NOT belong to the Chishti order?
q.x: Bahauddin Zakariya of Multan belonged to the Suhrawardi order.

q.s: Which of the following did NOT fight against the British in the Battle of Buxar (1764)?
q.x: At Buxar the British defeated Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Shah Alam II; Siraj-ud-Daula had died after Plassey (1757).

q.s: The Battle of Buxar was followed by the Treaty of:
q.x: The Treaty of Allahabad (1765) gave the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.

q.s: The 'White Mutiny' among Europeans in India was a reaction to the:
q.x: The Ilbert Bill (1883) under Ripon let Indian judges try Europeans and provoked the 'White Mutiny'.

q.s: The Raleigh Commission (1902) appointed under Lord Curzon dealt with:
q.x: Raleigh - universities; Scott-Moncrieff - irrigation; Frazer - police.

q.s: Which of the following commissions was NOT appointed during the viceroyalty of Lord Curzon?
q.x: The Hunter Commission on education was appointed under Ripon in 1882.

q.s: The Royal Titles Act of 1876, which gave Queen Victoria the title 'Kaiser-i-Hind', was passed during the viceroyalty of:
q.x: Lytton's viceroyalty saw the Royal Titles Act, the Delhi Durbar of 1877, and the Arms and Vernacular Press Acts (1878).

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a measure of Lord Lytton's viceroyalty?
q.x: The Ilbert Bill belongs to Ripon's time; Lytton passed the VPA and Arms Act in 1878.

q.s: The Permanent Settlement of 1793 was introduced by Lord Cornwallis with the help of:
q.x: John Shore helped plan it; Munro was linked with the Ryotwari and Holt Mackenzie with the Mahalwari system.

q.s: Under the Permanent Settlement, the zamindar was required to pay to the Company:
q.x: The zamindar paid 10/11 of the rental and kept 1/11.

q.s: According to the Drain theory, the drain of wealth took the form of:
o: An excess of exports over imports
An excess of imports over exports
q.x: The drain appeared as an unrequited excess of exports over imports.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a component of the 'Drain of Wealth' from India?
o: Land revenue spent on irrigation within India
Guaranteed returns on British investment in railways
Interest on the public debt raised in Britain
q.x: Revenue spent within India was not a drain; home charges, interest and guaranteed returns were.

q.s: Which leader accepted the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms and formed the Liberal Federation?
q.x: Surendranath Banerjee's Moderates accepted the reforms; Das and Tilak rejected them, and Gandhi and Malaviya wanted a fair trial.

q.s: Henry Vivian Derozio, leader of the Young Bengal movement, taught at:
q.x: Derozio taught at Hindu College, Calcutta and was dismissed in 1831 for his radical teaching.

q.s: In the Madras Presidency, Brahmins who formed about 3% of the population held over 90% of government jobs. This contributed to the rise of the:
q.x: Brahmin dominance in jobs fed the non-Brahmin movement (Justice Party, 1916).

q.s: Which of the following journals was NOT started by B.R. Ambedkar?
q.x: Kudi Arasu was Periyar's journal; Mooknayak (1920) was Ambedkar's.

q.s: The Satyashodhak Samaj was founded in 1873 at:
q.x: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj at Pune on 24 September 1873.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with Jyotiba Phule?
q.x: The Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924) was founded by Ambedkar; Din Bandhu was the organ of Phule's Samaj.

q.s: The Theosophical Society set up its headquarters at Adyar (Madras) in:
q.x: It was founded at New York in 1875 and moved its headquarters to Adyar in 1882.

q.s: Jiddu Krishnamurti, identified by C.W. Leadbeater in 1909, was born at:
q.x: Krishnamurti was born at Madanapalle in 1895 and left the Theosophical Society in 1929.

q.s: The main aim of the Rajahmundry Social Reform Association (1878) was to promote:
q.x: Founded by Veeresalingam's circle in 1878, the first organised reform body in Andhra aimed mainly at widow remarriage.

q.s: The first autobiography in Telugu was written by:
q.x: Veeresalingam wrote the first Telugu autobiography and also first rendered Sanskrit dramas like Abhijnana Sakuntalam into Telugu.

q.s: Which of the following works was NOT written by Kandukuri Veeresalingam?
q.x: Kanyasulkam is Gurajada Apparao's play.

q.s: At which session did Annie Besant become the first woman President of the Indian National Congress?
q.x: She presided over the Calcutta session of 1917.

q.s: Annie Besant renamed the 'Madras Standard' as:
q.x: In 1914 she bought the Madras Standard and renamed it New India; Commonweal was her weekly.

q.s: Who was the first principal of the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental (MAO) College at Aligarh?
q.x: H.G.I. Siddons was the first principal; Theodore Beck succeeded him.

q.s: The MAO College founded by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan became Aligarh Muslim University in:
q.x: The college, modelled on Oxford and Cambridge, became AMU in 1920.

q.s: The first district association in the Madras Presidency, organised by Ramaswamy Gupta in 1892, was the:
q.x: The Krishna District Association (1892) was the first; its 1899 resolution led to the Krishna Patrika (1902).

q.s: Andhra Patrika (1908) was started by:
q.x: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao started Andhra Patrika; Krishna Patrika came out of the Krishna District Association.

q.s: Who was the first Muslim President of the Indian National Congress?
q.x: Badruddin Tyabji presided over the Madras session of 1887.

q.s: Who was the first European to become President of the Indian National Congress?
q.x: George Yule presided over the Allahabad session of 1888.

q.s: Mahatma Gandhi regarded which leader as his 'political guru'?
q.x: Gandhi acknowledged Gokhale as his political mentor and on his advice toured India after returning in 1915.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a method of mass mobilisation during the Swadeshi movement?
q.x: Salt satyagraha came in 1930; Swadeshi (1905), India's first mass movement, used jatras, melas and samitis.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Simon Commission is correct?
o: It was appointed by Ramsay MacDonald's Labour government.
Its official name was the Indian Statutory Commission.
q.x: Appointed in November 1927 by Baldwin's government, it had seven British members including Attlee and no Indian.

q.s: The Simon Commission was appointed in 1927 by the British government headed by:
q.x: It was appointed by Stanley Baldwin's Conservative government, with Birkenhead as Secretary of State.

q.s: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact, which paved the way for the Second Round Table Conference, was signed on:
q.x: The Pact was signed on 5 March 1931; Gandhi attended the Second RTC as the sole Congress representative.

q.s: Gandhi began the Dandi March from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930 with how many followers?
q.x: He set out with 78 followers and broke the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930.

q.s: Dandi, where Gandhi broke the salt law in 1930, is located in present-day:
q.x: Dandi is on the south Gujarat coast, then in Surat and now in Navsari district.

q.s: In the Individual Satyagraha of 1940-41, who was the first satyagrahi chosen by Gandhi?
q.x: Vinoba Bhave was the first, Nehru the second and Brahma Dutt the third.

q.s: Kasturba Gandhi died in detention in 1944 at:
q.x: Kasturba and Mahadev Desai died at the Aga Khan Palace, where their samadhis stand.

q.s: The Rampa rebellion led by Alluri Sitarama Raju lasted from:
q.x: The armed tribal rising of the Koyas and Konda Doras ran from August 1922 to May 1924.

q.s: The Rampa rebellion of Alluri Sitarama Raju drew its main support from the:
q.x: Its base was among the Koyas and Konda Doras of the Gudem hills.

q.s: Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, known for the Chirala-Perala movement, was introduced to Gandhi in London in 1915 by:
q.x: Coomaraswamy introduced him to Gandhi; Gopalakrishnayya was born at Penuganchiprolu in Krishna district.

q.s: Potti Sriramulu began his fast for a separate Andhra state on 19 October 1952 at the Madras house of:
q.x: He fasted at Bulusu Sambamurthy's house in Mylapore and died on 15 December 1952.

q.s: The Sribagh Pact (1937) between leaders of coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema was signed at the house of:
q.x: It was signed on 16 November 1937 at 'Sribagh', Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao's house in Madras.

q.s: The Sribagh Pact between the leaders of coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema was concluded in:
q.x: The Pact was concluded on 16 November 1937.

q.s: Pingali Venkayya showed his design of the national flag to Gandhi at the AICC session held in 1921 at:
q.x: He presented it at the Vijayawada (Bezawada) AICC in 1921.

q.s: Pingali Venkayya, designer of the national flag, was born at Bhatlapenumarru near:
q.x: He was born on 2 August 1876 at Bhatlapenumarru near Machilipatnam.

q.s: The Practical Trusteeship Formula, based on Gandhi's ideas, was drafted by:
q.x: Narhari Parikh and Kishorelal Mashruwala drafted it, proposing a minimum living wage and an income ceiling.

q.s: Who was the first Indian to be elected President of the Central Legislative Assembly in 1925?
q.x: Vithalbhai Patel was elected on 24 August 1925, succeeding Sir Frederick Whyte.

q.s: Pattabhi Sitaramayya was defeated by Subhas Chandra Bose in the contest for the Congress presidency of the session at:
q.x: Bose was unopposed at Haripura but defeated Pattabhi in 1939 for Tripuri.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of popular title and person is NOT correct?
o: Grand Old Man of India - Dadabhai Naoroji
q.x: Rashtraguru was Surendranath Banerjee.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT connected with the Hyderabad 'police action' (Operation Polo) of 1948?
q.x: Chaudhuri led the Indian forces, El Edroos was the Nizam's army chief and Razvi the Razakar leader; Candeth commanded Operation Vijay in Goa (1961).

q.s: Who was the first Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission?
q.x: Gulzarilal Nanda was the first Deputy Chairman; Nehru was Chairman.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Planning Commission and the NDC is correct?
o: The Planning Commission was set up on 15 March 1950 by an executive resolution.
The Planning Commission was set up by an Act of Parliament in 1950.
The National Development Council was set up in 1950 along with the Planning Commission.
The Plans were finally approved by the Finance Commission.
q.x: The Commission came by executive resolution on 15 March 1950; the NDC was set up on 6 August 1952 and gave final approval to the Plans.

q.s: The Andhra University Bill of 1925 was drafted by:
q.x: C.R. Reddy drafted the Bill, which A.P. Patro introduced on 20 August 1925.

q.s: Who was the first Leader of the Opposition in the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly?
q.x: Communist leader Puchalapalli Sundarayya was the first; Kalluri Subbarao was the first Deputy Speaker.

q.s: Who was the first Deputy Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: K.V. Ranga Reddy was Deputy Chief Minister in 1959-62.

q.s: Under the Nizam's farman of 1919 on Mulki rules, a person qualified as a local (Mulki) for jobs after residing in Hyderabad State for about:
q.x: The 1919 farman required about 15 years' residence.

q.s: Violations of the Gentlemen's Agreement of 1956 led to which agitation in 1969?
q.x: Violations over jobs, domicile and surplus funds led to the Jai Telangana agitation of 1969.

q.s: The Gentlemen's Agreement (1956) laid down a residence requirement for recruitment in Telangana of:
q.x: The Agreement set 12 years' residence as the domicile condition.

q.s: Ship-type coins of the Satavahanas, indicating maritime trade, are associated with:
q.x: Yajna Sri Satakarni issued ship coins; Pulumavi III was the last ruler in the Puranic list.

q.s: In the Satavahana period, the tax 'Karukara' was levied on:
q.x: Karukara was the tax on artisans and professionals; Bhaga was the king's share of the harvest.

q.s: The largest brick stupa in India is located at:
q.x: Kesariya in Bihar has the largest brick stupa; the 'Sakiyanam' relic casket came from Piprahwa.

q.s: Which of the following stupa sites is NOT located in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Kesariya, with the largest brick stupa, is in Bihar.

q.s: Gautami Balasri, mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni, gifted a cave vihara at Nasik to the:
q.x: Her Nasik vihara went to the Bhadrayaniyas; Pulomavi II gave a village to the Mahasanghikas at Karle.

q.s: In early Andhra society, the term 'Halikas' referred to:
q.x: Halikas were farmers; Selavaddikas were stone sculptors and Swarnakaras goldsmiths.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a site of the Amaravati school of art?
q.x: Mat (near Mathura) belongs to the Kushana Mathura school.

q.s: The Puranas refer to the Ikshvakus of Andhra as:
q.x: The Puranas call them Sriparvatiyas and Andhrabhrityas.

q.s: Tara bronzes and a Buddha footprint have been found at which Buddhist site of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Salihundam (Srikakulam) yielded them; Bojjannakonda has a monolithic Buddha in Dhyana mudra.

q.s: Which of the following Buddhist sites is NOT in north coastal Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Nagarjunakonda is in Palnadu, on the Krishna; the others are in the Visakhapatnam-Srikakulam region.

q.s: The Vishnukundins moved their capital from Amarapuri to:
q.x: They moved to Denduluru to check Pallava invasions; the Chikkulla plates were issued from there.

q.s: Which is the only temple of the Bikkavolu group still standing?
q.x: Golingeswara is the only one still standing; the ASI attributes the group to Gunaga Vijayaditya III.

q.s: The Bikkavolu temples in East Godavari district are attributed by the ASI to the Eastern Chalukya king:
q.x: The ASI attributes the group to Gunaga Vijayaditya III.

q.s: 'Prataparudra Charitramu' was written by:
q.x: Ekamranatha wrote it; Nalakirtikaumudi is by Agastya and Khazain-ul-Futuh by Amir Khusrau.

q.s: Which of the following works was NOT written by Amir Khusrau?
q.x: Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi is by Ziauddin Barani.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Sharqi kingdom of Jaunpur is correct?
o: Jaunpur was founded by Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
The Atala Mosque was built by Bibi Raje.
The Lal Darwaza Mosque was built by Ibrahim Shah Sharqi.
Malik Sarwar made Jaunpur independent in 1394.
q.x: Malik Sarwar (Malik-us-Sharq) made it independent in 1394; Firoz Tughlaq founded Jaunpur; Ibrahim Shah built the Atala Mosque and Bibi Raje the Lal Darwaza.

q.s: Under the Qutb Shahis, a 'Sarkar' was headed by the:
q.x: A Sarkar was under a Faujdar and a Pargana under a Tahsildar or Deshmukh.

q.s: The Battle of Padmanabham (1794) was fought between the British and the rulers of:
q.x: The Pusapati ruler of Vizianagaram, Vijayarama Raju II, fell fighting the British at Padmanabham.

q.s: In the Vijayanagara empire, the main source of state revenue was:
q.x: Land tax was the main source of revenue; Devadaya were temple lands.

q.s: The Sahasra Stambha (thousand-pillared) mandapa is a characteristic feature of temples built by the:
q.x: Vijayanagara temples, drawing on Chalukya and Chola styles, are marked by large pillared mandapas.

q.s: Kakatiya temples used which technique for their foundations?
q.x: Kakatiya builders used sand-filled foundations (sandbox technique) to resist earthquakes.

q.s: Who presided over the first session of the Nizam's Andhra Mahasabha held at Jogipet in 1930?
q.x: Suravaram Pratap Reddy presided at Jogipet (1930); Ravi Narayana Reddy's presidency at Bhuvanagiri (1944) brought communist control.

q.s: The Bhuvanagiri session (1944) of the Andhra Mahasabha, which brought it under communist control, was presided over by:
q.x: Ravi Narayana Reddy presided at Bhuvanagiri in 1944.

q.s: The All India Kisan Sabha was founded in April 1936 at:
q.x: It was founded at Lucknow (first called the All India Kisan Congress), with Sahajanand Saraswati as president.

q.s: Who is known as 'Rythu Bandhu' and the 'Father of the Indian Peasant Movement'?
q.x: Acharya N.G. Ranga, who ran the journals Praja Bandhu and Navayuga.

q.s: Gorky's novel 'Mother' was translated into Telugu as 'Amma' in 1934 by:
q.x: Krovvidi Lingaraju's Amma (1934) was an early landmark of leftist Telugu literature.

q.s: T. Gopichand won the Sahitya Akademi award for which novel?
q.x: Pandita Parameswara Sastri Veelunama won the award; Chivaraku Migiledi is by Buchi Babu.

q.s: The Andhra State Act, 1953 came into force on:
q.x: Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953 with Kurnool as capital; the Act largely reproduced the Wanchoo apportionment.

q.s: The Vignana Chandrika Mandali (1906), which published 'Andhrula Charitramu', was founded at Hyderabad by:
q.x: Komarraju Lakshmana Rao founded it with the Munagala Zamindar's support.

q.s: 'Andhrula Charitramu', published by the Vignana Chandrika Mandali in 1910, was written by:
q.x: Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao wrote Andhrula Charitramu.

q.s: Dalavai Chalapathi Rao, who received the Padma Shri in 2020, is an exponent of which art form?
q.x: Dalavai Chalapathi Rao is a leather puppeteer (Tholu Bommalata) from Anantapur district.

q.s: The Potti Sreeramulu Telugu University was established in:
q.x: Telugu University came in 1985; the AP Sahitya Akademi in 1957, Ravindra Bharathi in 1961 and the International Telugu Institute in 1975.

q.s: Which of the following Telugu writers did NOT receive the Jnanpith Award?
q.x: Viswanatha (1970), C. Narayana Reddy (1988) and Ravuri Bharadwaja (2012) won the Jnanpith; Jashuva did not.

q.s: C. Narayana Reddy received the Jnanpith Award in 1988 for:
q.x: Vishwambhara; Veyipadagalu is Viswanatha's and Paakudu Raallu is Ravuri Bharadwaja's.

q.s: 'Nallapoddu', the first collection of Dalit women's writing in Telugu, was edited by:
q.x: Gogu Syamala edited Nallapoddu; Neeli Meghalu (1993) was edited by Volga and others.

q.s: Which Constituent Assembly member from Andhra later became the Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
q.x: Ananthasayanam Ayyangar became Deputy Speaker and then Speaker; Pattabhi chaired the House Committee.

q.s: The Andhra Mahila Sabha was founded by:
q.x: Durgabai Deshmukh founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha (1937).

q.s: In the Buddha's time, Kapilavastu was the centre of which republic?
q.x: Shakya - Kapilavastu; Koliya - Ramagama; Bhagga - Sumsumaragiri; Kalama - Kesaputta.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a republic (gana-sangha) in the time of the Buddha?
q.x: Avanti was a monarchy (Mahajanapada) under Pradyota.

q.s: The Second Buddhist Council was held at:
q.x: Rajagriha hosted the First and Vaishali the Second; Vaishali was the capital of the Lichchhavis.

q.s: Kumrahar and Bulandibagh are excavated remains of the ancient city of:
q.x: Kumrahar and Bulandibagh are Pataliputra sites.

q.s: Which of the following temples is NOT located in Odisha?
q.x: The Virupaksha temple is at Hampi, Karnataka.

q.s: Which of the following communities of India follows a matrilineal system?
q.x: The Khasi, Jaintia and Garo of Meghalaya are matrilineal exceptions to the broadly patriarchal pattern.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a language family of India?
q.x: India's four families are Indo-Aryan, Dravidian, Austro-Asiatic and Tibeto-Burman.

q.s: In Redfield and Singer's typology of urbanisation, primary urbanisation is described as:
q.x: Primary urbanisation is orthogenetic (moral order around temples); secondary urbanisation is heterogenetic, technical and commercial.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Scheduled Tribes is correct?
o: The Lokur Committee (1965) laid down five tests for identifying STs.
The criteria for identifying STs are laid down in the Constitution.
The Lokur Committee was set up in 1975.
q.x: The criteria come from the Lokur Committee of 1965, not the Constitution; STs form 8.6% of the population.

q.s: According to Census 2011, Scheduled Tribes form what percentage of India's population?
q.x: STs form 8.6% of India's population; SCs form 16.6%.

q.s: 'Gabbilam', a landmark of Telugu Dalit poetry, was written by:
q.x: Gurram Jashuva wrote Gabbilam; Manda Krishna Madiga led the Madiga Dandora.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of social reformer and organisation is NOT correct?
o: Bhagya Reddy Varma - Jagan Mitra Mandali
Manda Krishna Madiga - Madiga Reservation Porata Samithi
q.x: The Harijan Sevak Sangh was founded by Gandhi (1932); Jashuva was a poet (Gabbilam).

q.s: The word 'Secular' was added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by the:
q.x: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity'.

q.s: The Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act, 1991 freezes the religious character of places of worship as it existed on:
q.x: The cut-off date is 15 August 1947.

q.s: The six dimensions of communalism, from assimilationist to secessionist, were identified by:
q.x: T.K. Oommen gave the six dimensions; Bipan Chandra described three stages of communalism.

q.s: Which law decriminalised attempted suicide in practice by presuming severe stress in such cases?
o: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016
q.x: The Mental Healthcare Act 2017 moved the approach from punishment under Sec. 309 IPC to health care.

q.s: According to Census 2011, India's child sex ratio (0-6 years) was:
q.x: CSR was 918 in 2011, down from 927 in 2001; the overall sex ratio was 943.

q.s: POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched on 8 March 2018 at:
q.x: It was launched at Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan; it was earlier called the National Nutrition Mission.

q.s: The idea of PURA (Providing Urban Amenities in Rural Areas), revived in the Rurban Mission, was given by:
q.x: PURA was Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam's idea; the Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission was launched at Kurubhat in 2016.

q.s: The Shyama Prasad Mukherji Rurban Mission was launched in February 2016 in which State?
q.x: It was launched at Kurubhat, Rajnandgaon district, Chhattisgarh.

q.s: Article 370 of the Indian Constitution was placed in which Part?
q.x: Article 370 was in Part XXI (temporary, transitional and special provisions); Part XVIII deals with emergencies.

q.s: The India-Pakistan war of 1965 was preceded by Pakistan's infiltration operation known as:
q.x: Operation Gibraltar (infiltration) and Operation Grand Slam (Akhnoor) led to the 1965 war.

q.s: The India-China war of 1962 was fought mainly in which two sectors?
q.x: It was fought in Aksai Chin (Ladakh) and NEFA; China declared a unilateral ceasefire on 21 November 1962.

q.s: The report that reviewed India's military failure in the 1962 war was the:
q.x: The Henderson Brooks-Bhagat Report; K. Subrahmanyam headed the Kargil Review Committee (1999).

q.s: In India, anti-dumping, countervailing and safeguard investigations are conducted by the:
q.x: The Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR) conducts them; the DGFT handles foreign trade policy.

q.s: Which of the following statements about trade barriers is correct?
o: Phytosanitary rules and technical standards are non-tariff barriers.
Anti-dumping inquiries in India are conducted by the DGFT.
Countervailing duties are non-tariff barriers on exports.
q.x: Phytosanitary rules and technical standards are NTBs; trade remedy inquiries are by the DGTR.

q.s: India's first compulsory licence under its patent law was granted in 2012 in the case of:
q.x: Natco got a compulsory licence for Bayer's cancer drug Nexavar in 2012.

q.s: India amended its Patents Act to allow product patents, to meet TRIPS obligations, in:
q.x: Product patents came with the 2005 amendment; the GI Act was enacted in 1999.

q.s: The BIMSTEC Charter was adopted at the 5th Summit held in 2022, hosted by:
q.x: Sri Lanka hosted the 5th (virtual) Summit at Colombo in 2022.

q.s: The European Union was created by the:
q.x: Maastricht created the EU; the Treaty of Rome set up the EEC.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the European Union?
q.x: Norway is not an EU member; Croatia (2013) is the latest member.

q.s: The United States withdrew from the Iran nuclear deal (JCPOA) in 2018 under President:
q.x: The JCPOA was concluded in 2015; the US withdrew in 2018 under Trump.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT among the P5+1 countries that negotiated the JCPOA with Iran?
q.x: P5+1 = USA, UK, France, Russia, China and Germany.

q.s: Under the NPT, Nuclear Weapon States are those that tested a nuclear device before:
q.x: The cut-off date is 1 January 1967.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the NPT is correct?
o: It was signed in 1970 and entered into force in 1975.
Its Review Conferences are held every ten years.
India signed it in 1968 as a non-nuclear state.
q.x: Signed in 1968, in force from 1970, extended indefinitely in 1995; Review Conferences every five years; India has not signed it.

q.s: The Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR) was set up in:
q.x: MTCR (1987) controls missiles and drones capable of carrying 500 kg over 300 km; the NSG dates from 1975.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a multilateral export control regime?
q.x: The CTBT bans nuclear tests; the NSG, MTCR, Wassenaar and Australia Group are export control regimes.

q.s: About half of India's crude oil imports pass through which strait?
q.x: About half pass through the Strait of Hormuz; India imports about 85-88% of its crude requirement.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four 'A's of India's energy security?
q.x: The four A's are Availability, Accessibility, Affordability and Acceptability.

q.s: The procedure for amendment of the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the Constitution of:
q.x: The amendment procedure is from South Africa; the Concurrent List is from Australia.

q.s: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution was NOT borrowed from Britain?
q.x: Judicial review comes from the USA.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State?
q.x: Article 50, a Directive Principle.

q.s: Under the Indian Councils Act 1909, S.P. Sinha became the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council as:
q.x: S.P. Sinha joined as Law Member.

q.s: Bicameralism at the Centre was first introduced in British India by the:
q.x: The 1919 Act created the Central Legislative Assembly and the Council of State.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Government of India Act 1919?
o: Separation of central and provincial budgets
q.x: The 1919 Act gave direct elections on a limited property, tax and education franchise, not adult franchise.

q.s: The 'Essential Religious Practices' test originated in which Supreme Court case?
q.x: Shirur Mutt (1954) originated the test and defined 'religious denomination'.

q.s: In Rev. Stanislaus v. State of Madhya Pradesh (1977), the Supreme Court held that:
o: Polygamy is not an essential religious practice
Religious denominations may manage their own affairs
The right to propagate religion does not include a right to convert
q.x: Stanislaus held propagation is not a right to convert, upholding the Orissa and MP anti-conversion Acts.

q.s: Which of the following can the Governor NOT do with a Money Bill passed by the State Legislature?
o: Return it to the Legislature for reconsideration
Reserve it for the consideration of the President
q.x: A Money Bill cannot be returned for reconsideration; the Governor may assent, withhold assent or reserve it for the President.

q.s: In the passage of an ordinary Bill, the committee stage and clause-by-clause consideration take place at the:
q.x: The second reading covers general discussion, committee stage and clause-by-clause consideration; the third reading votes on the Bill as a whole.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court fix 24 April 1973 as the cut-off date after which Ninth Schedule laws are open to basic structure review?
q.x: Waman Rao (1981) fixed the Kesavananda date; I.R. Coelho (2007) confirmed there is no blanket immunity.

q.s: The word 'Cabinet' was inserted into Article 352 of the Constitution by the:
q.x: The 44th Amendment required a written Cabinet decision for a national emergency, inserting 'Cabinet' in Art. 352(3).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Union Council of Ministers?
q.x: Parliamentary Secretaries are not members of the Council of Ministers.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the qualifications for membership of Parliament?
q.x: Art. 84 - qualifications; Art. 83 - duration of the Houses; Art. 100 - voting and quorum.

q.s: The six-year term of members of the Rajya Sabha is fixed by:
o: The Rules of Procedure of the Rajya Sabha
The Representation of the People Act, 1951
q.x: The term is fixed by the RPA, 1951; a casual-vacancy member serves only the rest of the predecessor's term.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Rajya Sabha is correct?
o: Its members' six-year term is fixed by the Constitution.
It is dissolved every six years.
A member elected to a casual vacancy serves a full fresh term.
In 1952 the members to retire first were chosen by lottery.
q.x: The term is fixed by the RPA, 1951; casual-vacancy members serve the rest of the term; the House is permanent.

q.s: Under which Article does the Speaker of the Lok Sabha decide finally whether a Bill is a Money Bill?
q.x: Art. 110(3) makes the Speaker's decision final; Art. 118(4) provides for the Speaker presiding over a joint sitting.

q.s: The Parliamentary Committee on the Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes consists of how many members?
q.x: It has 30 members - 20 from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha; a Minister cannot be a member.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a financial committee of Parliament?
o: Committee on the Welfare of SCs and STs
q.x: The three financial committees are PAC, Estimates and Public Undertakings.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court allow limited judicial review of the pardoning power on grounds of mala fides or irrelevant considerations?
q.x: Epuru Sudhakar (2006), arising from Andhra Pradesh; Kehar Singh held there is no right to an oral hearing.

q.s: Who alone can grant a pardon for a sentence passed by a court-martial?
q.x: Only the President (Art. 72) can pardon a court-martial sentence; the Governor has no such power.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Indian and British parliamentary systems is correct?
o: Both are based on the sovereignty of Parliament.
Indian ministers, like British ministers, are legally responsible for acts of the Head of State.
India, like Britain, has an institutionalised shadow cabinet.
The Indian Prime Minister may belong to either House of Parliament.
q.x: The Indian PM may belong to either House; India has no parliamentary sovereignty, no shadow cabinet and no legal responsibility of ministers.

q.s: As of 2022, the largest share of pending cases in India was in:
q.x: About 87.4% of over 4.7 crore pending cases were in subordinate courts; about 12.4% were in the High Courts.

q.s: Who described Indian federalism as 'bargaining federalism'?
q.x: Morris-Jones; Paul Appleby called it 'extremely federal' and Alexandrowicz 'a case sui generis'.

q.s: Who described India as 'extremely federal'?
q.x: Paul Appleby; K. Santhanam stressed the unitary bias from financial dependence and the Planning Commission.

q.s: When an entry in the Union List overlaps with an entry in the Concurrent List, which prevails?
q.x: The Union List prevails (Art. 246); the Concurrent List now has 52 entries against 47 originally.

q.s: For disaster funds under the 16th Finance Commission, the Centre-State sharing ratio for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States is:
q.x: NE and Himalayan States share 90:10; other States share 75:25.

q.s: Amnesty International, founded in London in 1961, was founded by:
q.x: Peter Benenson founded Amnesty; it won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1977.

q.s: Which of the following statements about human rights bodies is correct?
o: Amnesty International was founded in Geneva.
The UN Human Rights Prize is awarded by the Human Rights Council.
Human Rights Watch is based in New York.
Amnesty International won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1987.
q.x: Amnesty was founded in London (1961) and won the Nobel in 1977; the UN prize is given by the General Assembly.

q.s: Article 26 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights deals with the right to:
q.x: UDHR Art. 26 - education; Art. 3 - life, liberty and security; Art. 12 - privacy; Art. 23 - work.

q.s: The 16-point guidelines on investigating police encounter killings were laid down in:
o: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal
Prakash Singh v. Union of India
Nilabati Behera v. State of Orissa
q.x: PUCL (2014) laid down the encounter guidelines; D.K. Basu (1997) dealt with arrest and detention.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a federal feature of the Indian Constitution?
q.x: All India Services, serving both Union and States, are a unitary feature.

q.s: The Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State relations was set up in 1983 by the government of:
q.x: Indira Gandhi's government set it up in 1983.

q.s: The Sri Krishna Commission inquired into the:
q.x: Justice B.N. Srikrishna probed the 1992-93 Mumbai riots; the Liberhan Commission probed the Babri Masjid demolition.

q.s: The First Administrative Reforms Commission recommended the setting up of an Inter-State Council under:
q.x: Article 263 provides for the Inter-State Council; the ARC's study team on Centre-State relations was headed by M.C. Setalvad.

q.s: The 14th Finance Commission raised the States' share in the divisible pool of central taxes from 32% to:
q.x: The 14th FC (Y.V. Reddy) raised it to 42%; the 15th and 16th FCs fixed 41%.

q.s: The 16th Finance Commission, covering 2026-31, is chaired by:
q.x: Arvind Panagariya; the 15th FC was chaired by N.K. Singh.

q.s: Political parties were first mentioned in the Constitution through the Tenth Schedule, added by the:
q.x: The 52nd Amendment (1985) added the anti-defection Tenth Schedule.

q.s: Which of the following Lok Sabha constituencies of Andhra Pradesh is NOT reserved for Scheduled Castes?
q.x: AP's SC seats are Amalapuram, Bapatla, Chittoor and Tirupati; Nellore is a general seat.

q.s: Which of the following Lok Sabha seats of Telangana is reserved for Scheduled Tribes?
q.x: Adilabad and Mahabubabad are ST seats; Nagarkurnool, Peddapalle and Warangal are SC seats.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Delimitation Commission is correct?
o: Its orders can be modified by the Lok Sabha.
Its nodal ministry is the Ministry of Home Affairs.
It does not fix reserved seats for SCs and STs.
Its orders cannot be questioned in any court and cannot be modified by Parliament.
q.x: Its orders have the force of law and cannot be modified by the Lok Sabha or an Assembly; it also fixes SC/ST seats, and the Law Ministry is the nodal ministry.

q.s: The '3Fs' of devolution to Panchayati Raj Institutions refer to:
q.x: Funds, Functions and Functionaries; in practice funds are mostly tied and functionaries report to line departments.

q.s: 'Nigha', an app launched by Andhra Pradesh in 2020, was meant for:
o: Citizens reporting poll irregularities in local body elections
q.x: Nigha let citizens report money and liquor distribution in local polls; Mee Seva is the single-window counter.

q.s: How many Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) are there in India?
q.x: There are 75 PVTGs in 18 States and 1 UT; Andhra Pradesh has 12, including the Chenchu.

q.s: The slogan 'Minimum Government, Maximum Governance' stands for:
o: A larger state machinery with more ministries
A leaner state that governs more effectively
q.x: It means a leaner State that governs better, used since 2014.

q.s: India's first integrated citizen service centres, 'e-Seva', were launched in Andhra Pradesh in:
q.x: e-Seva came in 2001; MeeSeva later offered single-window certificates, and AP FiberNet came in 2017.

q.s: The Appiko movement for forest conservation took place in 1983 in:
q.x: Appiko was in Karnataka; Chipko (1973) was in Uttarakhand and MKSS (1990) in Rajasthan.

q.s: The anti-arrack movement of 1992 in Andhra Pradesh began at Dubagunta village in which district?
q.x: It began at Dubagunta in Nellore district.

q.s: Which of the following States is NOT covered under the Atal Bhujal Yojana?
q.x: The seven States are Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, MP, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and UP.

q.s: The Krishna and Godavari River Management Boards were constituted under which Section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
q.x: Section 85 covers the constitution and functions of the Boards; Section 87 their jurisdiction over notified projects.

q.s: The Girijan Cooperative Corporation of Andhra Pradesh is headquartered at:
q.x: The GCC, which runs MSP for minor forest produce, is at Visakhapatnam.

q.s: Under PESA, 1996, ownership of minor forest produce is vested in the:
q.x: PESA gives the Gram Sabha/Panchayat ownership of minor forest produce.

q.s: The 14th WTO Ministerial Conference (MC14) was held in March 2026 at:
q.x: MC14 was at Yaounde, Cameroon; MC12 (2022) was at Geneva and MC13 (2024) at Abu Dhabi.

q.s: The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies was adopted at the WTO Ministerial Conference held in June 2022 at:
q.x: MC12 at Geneva adopted the Fisheries Subsidies Agreement and the COVID-19 TRIPS waiver.

q.s: The Gender Development Index (GDI) and Gender Empowerment Measure (GEM) were introduced in the Human Development Report of:
q.x: HDR 1995; the Human Poverty Index came in 1997 and the planetary pressures-adjusted HDI in 2020.

q.s: According to Census 2011, which State has the largest number of statutory towns?
q.x: UP has the most statutory towns; Tamil Nadu has the most towns overall.

q.s: PAHAL, the direct benefit transfer scheme for LPG subsidy, is run by the:
o: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
q.x: PAHAL (national from 1 January 2015) is run by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

q.s: Which of the following statements about PAHAL is correct?
o: It is run by the Ministry of Rural Development.
It transfers the LPG subsidy directly to the consumer's bank account.
It was launched in all districts on 1 January 2013.
q.x: PAHAL (DBTL) began in 54 districts in November 2014 and nationally on 1 January 2015, under the Petroleum Ministry.

q.s: Phase II of the Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) is known as the:
q.x: Phase II (2020-25) is ODF Plus: sustaining ODF status with solid and liquid waste management.

q.s: The Swachh Vayu Survekshan is conducted under the:
q.x: MoEFCC conducts it under NCAP; SBM-Urban 2.0 was launched on 1 October 2021.

q.s: Which State has the highest share of stunted children as per the Poshan Tracker (July 2025)?
q.x: Uttar Pradesh (48.8%); MP has the highest share of underweight children and Bihar of wasted children.

q.s: The new GDP series released by MoSPI on 27 February 2026 uses which base year?
q.x: The new series moved the base from 2011-12 to 2022-23.

q.s: Under the Make in India initiative, the target share of manufacturing in India's GDP is:
q.x: The target is 25% of GDP; the deadline was extended from 2022 to 2025 and the target was not met.

q.s: Which survey of MoSPI provides the official estimates of unemployment in India, including State-wise rates?
q.x: The PLFS; in 2023-24 Andhra Pradesh's rate was above the national rate owing to urban and youth unemployment.

q.s: The First National Income Committee (1949-51) was chaired by:
q.x: Mahalanobis chaired it; it estimated 1948-49 national income at Rs 8,710 crore and per capita income at Rs 225.

q.s: Life expectancy in India at the time of Independence was about:
q.x: Life expectancy in 1947 was only about 32 years.

q.s: Which of the following statements about capital formation and development is correct?
o: Capital formation always raises output whatever the conditions.
Capital formation may fail to raise output when capital is idle or complementary skills are missing.
Human resource development lies outside the scope of development.
Capital formation depends only on savings, not on financial institutions.
q.x: Idle or misused capital or a lack of complementary inputs such as skills limit the effect of capital formation; human resources are part of development.

q.s: The inequality reports released every year at the World Economic Forum in Davos are published by:
q.x: Oxfam publishes the Davos reports; the World Inequality Report is by the World Inequality Lab (Paris School of Economics).

q.s: Wealth tax in India was abolished with effect from:
q.x: Wealth tax was abolished from 1 April 2016; estate duty was abolished in 1985.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to prevent the concentration of wealth and means of production?
q.x: Art. 39(c) is on preventing concentration of wealth; Art. 38(2) is on minimising inequalities in income.

q.s: The concept of the 'natural rate of unemployment' is associated with:
q.x: Friedman; Phillips showed the inverse inflation-unemployment relation (1958) and Okun linked unemployment to output.

q.s: The inverse relationship between the rate of inflation and the rate of unemployment is shown by the:
q.x: A.W. Phillips (1958).

q.s: Which of the following is regarded as a failure of planning in India?
q.x: Regional disparities and poorly implemented land reforms persist; the Plans averaged about 4.5% growth against about 1% before Independence.

q.s: Which Five Year Plan began immediately after the stabilisation and structural adjustment reforms of 1991?
q.x: The Eighth Plan (1992-97); IMF-World Bank programmes typically required currency devaluation.

q.s: The Planning Commission of India was set up on 15 March 1950 by:
q.x: It was created by a Cabinet resolution and was a non-constitutional body; NITI Aayog replaced it in 2015.

q.s: Under the zero-MDR regime in India, merchants pay no Merchant Discount Rate on transactions made through:
q.x: RuPay debit card and BHIM-UPI transactions carry zero MDR; the cost falls on banks and payment providers.

q.s: The Currency Note Press of the Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India is located at:
q.x: Nashik; the Bank Note Press is at Dewas and the RBI-owned BRBNMPL presses at Mysuru and Salboni.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a location of a mint of the Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India?
q.x: The four mints are at Mumbai, Noida, Kolkata and Hyderabad; Dewas has the Bank Note Press.

q.s: Which committee recommended opening the insurance sector to private companies with an independent regulator?
q.x: The R.N. Malhotra Committee (1993-94); the IRDA Act followed in 1999.

q.s: The Unit Trust of India (UTI) was set up in:
q.x: UTI 1964; LIC 1956; GIC 1972; SEBI was set up in 1988 and became statutory in 1992.

q.s: SEBI was given statutory status in:
q.x: SEBI was set up in 1988 and became a statutory body in 1992.

q.s: Scheduled banks in India are those listed in the:
o: First Schedule of the Banking Regulation Act
Third Schedule of the Companies Act
Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934
q.x: Scheduled banks are in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act and need paid-up capital and reserves of at least Rs 5 lakh.

q.s: The Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) was formed in:
q.x: DICGC was formed in 1978 by merging the DIC and the Credit Guarantee Corporation of India.

q.s: The prudential norms known as IRACP for banks were introduced in India from:
q.x: IRACP (Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning) came from 1992; interest on an NPA is booked only when received.

q.s: Which of the following statements about bank prudential norms is correct?
o: Interest on an NPA is booked as income only when actually received.
A higher Provision Coverage Ratio shows a weaker bank.
Interest on an NPA is booked as income when it falls due.
q.x: Income on NPAs is recognised only on receipt; a higher PCR shows a more resilient bank.

q.s: The practice of granting fresh loans to a defaulting borrower to repay old loans, thereby hiding defaults, is known as:
q.x: Evergreening hid defaults; aggressive lending in 2010-15 to infrastructure, steel and power also raised NPAs.

q.s: Under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, the resolution plan in a CIRP is approved by the:
o: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India
q.x: The Committee of Creditors votes on the plan; the outer limit for CIRP is 330 days.

q.s: The minimum amount of default required to trigger insolvency proceedings under the IBC is:
q.x: The threshold was raised from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 1 crore in 2020.

q.s: Which of the following fertilisers is NOT covered under the Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) scheme?
q.x: NBS (from 1 April 2010) covers decontrolled P&K fertilisers; urea is outside it.

q.s: Exporting a product at a price lower than its price in the home market is called:
q.x: That is dumping; a countervailing duty offsets foreign subsidies.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a trade remedy measure under WTO rules?
q.x: Rules of origin decide a product's national source; the other three are trade remedies.

q.s: The first 'Foreign Trade Policy' of India (replacing the EXIM Policy name) covered the period:
q.x: The FTP name came in 2004-09; the first EXIM Policy was 1985-88.

q.s: India recorded a record gross FDI inflow of $94.6 billion in which financial year?
q.x: FY 2025-26; net FDI peaked at $44 billion in 2020-21 and stays weak because of repatriation and outward FDI.

q.s: In 2024-25, India's horticulture output compared with its foodgrain output was:
q.x: Horticulture (367.72 MT) exceeded foodgrains (357.73 MT) owing to much higher yields per hectare.

q.s: The National Food Security Act, 2013 covers up to what share of the rural population?
q.x: Up to 75% rural and 50% urban - about two-thirds of the population.

q.s: The National Food Security Act, 2013 is administered by the:
o: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Department of Food and Public Distribution
q.x: The Department of Food and Public Distribution (Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution).

q.s: Command Area Development and Water Management falls under which component of the PMKSY?
q.x: It is under Har Khet Ko Pani; Per Drop More Crop moved to RKVY in December 2021.

q.s: The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (2020) provides interest subvention of 3% on loans up to:
q.x: Loans up to Rs 2 crore get 3% subvention; credit guarantee is through CGTMSE in a Rs 1 lakh crore facility.

q.s: Bt cotton was approved for commercial cultivation in India in 2002 by the:
q.x: The Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee (GEAC) approved it.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the three pillars of the WTO Agreement on Agriculture?
q.x: The three pillars are market access, domestic support and export subsidies; IPRs fall under TRIPS.

q.s: Which status gives Central Public Sector Enterprises the greatest financial autonomy?
q.x: Maharatna, for larger CPSEs meant to become global giants, gives more autonomy than Navratna.

q.s: Disinvestment receipts in the Union Budget are shown under:
q.x: They are Miscellaneous Capital Receipts (non-debt capital receipts).

q.s: In the IMD World Competitiveness Ranking 2025, India was ranked:
q.x: 41st; India was 68th in the last WEF Global Competitiveness Index (2019).

q.s: In the State Business Reform Action Plan ranking of 2016, which States were jointly ranked first?
q.x: AP and Telangana were joint first in 2016; AP was first again in the 2019 ranking.

q.s: The Index of Services Production (ISP) of MoSPI is the services-sector counterpart of the:
q.x: The ISP is the services counterpart of the IIP; it is a monthly index released within 60 days.

q.s: Among the old 13 districts of Andhra Pradesh, which had the lowest multidimensional poverty?
q.x: West Godavari (2.42%), a prosperous canal-irrigated delta district.

q.s: Which party left the NDA in 2018 over the issue of Special Category Status for Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: The TDP left the NDA in 2018 over SCS.

q.s: The largest source of Andhra Pradesh's own tax revenue is:
q.x: SGST is the largest (about 37% in 2025-26 BE); State excise yields more than stamps and registration.

q.s: According to the CAG, in 2015-16 own tax revenue formed about what share of Andhra Pradesh's revenue receipts?
q.x: Own tax was about 45% of revenue receipts in 2015-16.

q.s: Special Category Status was first granted to States in 1969. Which of the following was NOT among the first States to receive it?
q.x: J&K, Assam and Nagaland were the first; Himachal Pradesh got it later (1970-71).

q.s: For Special Category States, Centrally Sponsored Schemes are funded by the Centre and the State in the ratio:
q.x: SCS States get 90:10; other States 60:40.

q.s: Under Andhra Pradesh's Annadata Sukhibhava-PM Kisan scheme, the total annual assistance per farmer family is:
q.x: Rs 20,000 a year (including PM-Kisan); Rs 13,500 was the old YSR Rythu Bharosa amount.

q.s: As per the White Paper on Agriculture (December 2018), Andhra Pradesh ranked first in the country in the production of:
q.x: AP ranked first in poultry and fifth in milk; livestock and horticulture were named growth engines.

q.s: Which agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh receives the lowest rainfall?
q.x: The Scarce Rainfall Zone (Kurnool, Anantapuramu) lies in the rain-shadow region and gets the least rain.

q.s: Which agro-climatic zone of Andhra Pradesh is NOT correctly paired with its feature?
o: High Altitude and Tribal Zone - deltaic alluvium
North Coastal Zone - high rainfall and laterite soils
Scarce Rainfall Zone - red and black soils
q.x: The High Altitude and Tribal Zone has hill soils, not deltaic alluvium.

q.s: Under the AP Industrial Development Policy 2020-23, 16.2% of APIIC plots were reserved for entrepreneurs belonging to:
q.x: 16.2% of plots were for SC entrepreneurs; the 25% land rebate was capped at Rs 20 lakh.

q.s: Funding a start-up from the founder's own savings and revenue is known as:
q.x: Bootstrapping; angel investors put in their own money at the seed stage and crowdfunding raises small sums from many people.

q.s: A solar eclipse occurs on:
o: Any day of the lunar month
q.x: At new moon the Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth; a lunar eclipse occurs at full moon.

q.s: The longest total solar eclipse of the 21st century occurred on:
q.x: 22 July 2009; 15 January 2010 was the longest annular eclipse.

q.s: The Sun's diameter is about how many times that of the Earth?
q.x: About 109 times; the Sun holds about 99.8% of the solar system's mass.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Sun is NOT correct?
o: It holds about 99.8% of the mass of the solar system.
Its centre is in the solid state.
Its energy comes from nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium.
Its diameter is about 109 times that of the Earth.
q.x: Even its centre is gaseous (plasma).

q.s: The weight of an object on the Earth's surface is the greatest at the:
q.x: Weight is greatest at the poles (nearer the centre, no centrifugal effect) and least at the Equator.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the shape of the Earth is correct?
o: Weight of a body is least at the poles.
The poles are nearer to the Earth's centre than the Equator.
The equatorial radius is smaller than the polar radius.
Centrifugal force due to rotation is greatest at the poles.
q.x: The poles are about 21 km nearer the centre, so g and weight are greatest there.

q.s: The length of the coastline of Andhra Pradesh is about:
q.x: About 1,053 km, the second-longest after Gujarat.

q.s: The Earth's axis is inclined to the plane of its orbit at an angle of:
q.x: 66 1/2 degrees to the orbital plane (23 1/2 degrees from the perpendicular); seasons result from revolution with this tilt.

q.s: Basic (mafic) lava, which is runny, typically builds:
q.x: Basic lava flows far and forms shield volcanoes; viscous acidic lava does not flow far.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of acidic (felsic) lava?
q.x: Acidic lava is viscous and does not flow far; it solidifies quickly.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a desert (aeolian) landform?
q.x: A drumlin is a glacial landform.

q.s: The Jura mountains lie on the border of:
q.x: The Jura are on the France-Switzerland border; the Balkan range is in Bulgaria.

q.s: Mount Cook (Aoraki) is the highest peak of the:
q.x: The Southern Alps of New Zealand; the Great Dividing Range runs along Australia's east coast.

q.s: Tropical cyclones over the Bay of Bengal and the Arabian Sea are named by:
q.x: RSMC New Delhi (IMD), one of six WMO RSMCs, names cyclones for the North Indian Ocean.

q.s: Most of the atmospheric ozone (about 90%) is found in the:
q.x: About 90% of ozone is in the stratosphere; column ozone is measured in Dobson Units.

q.s: Which of the following statements about ozone is correct?
o: About 90% of atmospheric ozone lies in the troposphere.
One Dobson Unit equals 1 mm of pure ozone at 0 degrees C and 1 atm.
In the Chapman cycle, ultraviolet radiation splits O2 and the oxygen atoms combine with O2 to form O3.
Ozone is formed mainly by lightning.
q.x: About 90% of ozone is stratospheric and one DU is 0.01 mm of pure ozone.

q.s: The Siliguri corridor, known as the 'Chicken's Neck', lies in which State?
q.x: It lies in West Bengal between Nepal and Bangladesh and links the North-East with the rest of India.

q.s: The Line of Control in Jammu and Kashmir was established under the:
q.x: The Simla Agreement (1972) between India and Pakistan turned the ceasefire line into the LoC.

q.s: Which boundary line shows Aksai Chin as part of India?
q.x: The Johnson Line places Aksai Chin in India; the McDonald Line places it in China.

q.s: Nanga Parbat lies at the western end of which range of the Himalayas?
q.x: Nanga Parbat (about 8,126 m) is at the western end of the Greater Himalaya (Himadri).

q.s: Which of the following glaciers is NOT located in Uttarakhand?
q.x: Zemu glacier is in Sikkim.

q.s: Sriharikota island, the site of India's satellite launch centre, separates the sea from:
q.x: Sriharikota in Tirupati district lies between Pulicat Lake and the Bay of Bengal.

q.s: Which of the following islands is NOT located in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Piram is in the Gulf of Khambhat, Gujarat.

q.s: Arma Konda (Sitamma Konda), among the highest peaks of the Eastern Ghats in Andhra Pradesh, is located in:
q.x: Arma Konda is in Chintapalli, Alluri Sitharama Raju district; Deomali is in Koraput, Odisha.

q.s: The IMD Cyclone Warning Centre of Andhra Pradesh is located at:
q.x: It is at Visakhapatnam.

q.s: The Sutlej river enters India through which pass?
q.x: The Sutlej rises at Rakas Tal in Tibet and enters India at Shipki La in Himachal Pradesh.

q.s: Which of the following rivers does NOT rise in Tibet?
q.x: The Beas rises at Beas Kund near Rohtang Pass in Himachal Pradesh.

q.s: Which is the largest soil group in India by area?
q.x: Alluvial soils cover about 45.6%; black soils about 16.6%; red soil is third.

q.s: How many major soil types are recognised by the ICAR in India?
q.x: The ICAR recognises eight major soil types.

q.s: The predominant soil type of Karnataka is:
q.x: Karnataka has mostly red soil, followed by black soil.

q.s: As per ISFR 2023, the largest forest density class in Andhra Pradesh is:
q.x: Open Forest became the largest class in ISFR 2023; scrub (canopy below 10%) is not counted as forest cover.

q.s: The Rashtriya Barh Ayog (National Flood Commission) was set up in:
q.x: It was set up in 1976 and reported in 1980; flood control is a State subject.

q.s: Which of the following statements about flood management in India is correct?
o: Flood control is a State subject; the Centre gives technical and financial help.
Flood control is a Union subject.
The Rashtriya Barh Ayog was set up in 1990.
FMBAP is funded entirely by the States.
q.x: Flood control is a State subject; the Centre assists through FMBAP; the Ayog came in 1976.

q.s: Which country is the largest producer of crude oil in the world?
q.x: The USA is the largest crude oil producer.

q.s: The world's largest producer of iodine is:
q.x: Chile leads, with Japan second.

q.s: Monazite sands are an important source of:
q.x: Monazite gives thorium and rare earths; rutile and ilmenite are titanium ores.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of ore and metal is NOT correct?
q.x: Rutile is an ore of titanium.

q.s: Which State has the largest reserves of haematite iron ore in India?
q.x: Odisha leads in haematite; Karnataka holds about 72% of magnetite reserves.

q.s: Which country is the largest producer and exporter of iron ore in the world?
q.x: Australia; India ranks about fourth.

q.s: Most of India's coal is found in rocks of the:
q.x: Coal is Gondwana; the Cuddapah system has no coal and the Vindhyans hold the Panna diamonds.

q.s: India's three-stage nuclear power programme was formulated to make use of India's large reserves of:
q.x: Homi Bhabha's programme aims at thorium, found in monazite beach sands of Kerala, TN, AP and Odisha.

q.s: Which of the following statements about thorium in India is correct?
o: India holds about 60% of the world's thorium.
India's thorium is found mainly in the coal seams of the Damodar valley.
India's thorium occurs mainly in monazite beach sands of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
q.x: India has about 25% of world thorium, in monazite sands.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a kharif crop?
q.x: Gram is a rabi pulse.

q.s: 'Tungro' disease of rice is caused by a:
q.x: Tungro is viral; black rust of wheat is caused by the fungus Puccinia.

q.s: 'White bud' of maize is caused by deficiency of:
q.x: White bud of maize is due to zinc deficiency; ear cockle of wheat is caused by the nematode Anguina tritici.

q.s: The National Food Security Mission was renamed the National Food Security and Nutrition Mission in:
q.x: Launched in 2007-08, it added nutri-cereals in 2018-19 and was renamed in 2024-25; oilseeds have a separate mission.

q.s: Raising a crop from the stubble of the previous harvest is called:
q.x: Ratoon cropping is regrowth from the stubble, common in sugarcane; relay cropping sows the next crop into the standing crop.

q.s: Gypsum is applied to which crop to help pod filling?
q.x: Groundnut needs light sandy loam and calcium (gypsum) for pods.

q.s: Which of the following plantation crops is grown under shade and is sensitive to frost?
q.x: Coffee needs 15-28 degrees C with shade and no frost.

q.s: Which State leads India in turmeric production?
q.x: Maharashtra leads, followed by Tamil Nadu and Telangana.

q.s: The headquarters of the Tobacco Board of India is located at:
q.x: The Tobacco Board is at Guntur, also AP's chilli-trade hub.

q.s: Which mode of transport carries about 95% of India's trade by volume?
q.x: Shipping carries about 95% by volume and 68% by value.

q.s: Which country became the 11th member of ASEAN in 2025?
q.x: Timor-Leste joined in 2025.

q.s: Which of the following statements about trade blocs is correct?
o: India is a founder member of RCEP.
Chile is a full member of Mercosur.
India stayed out of RCEP when it was finalised in 2019.
q.x: India withdrew from RCEP in 2019; Chile is only an associate member of Mercosur; ASEAN has 11 members.

q.s: The west coast of India has more natural harbours than the east coast mainly because it is:
o: Submerged and indented with deep water near the shore
q.x: The submerged, indented west coast has deep water near the shore; the east coast has broad deltas and a shallow shelf.

q.s: Which of the following major ports is NOT on the east coast of India?
q.x: Kochi is on the west coast.

q.s: Which major port handled the largest cargo in India in FY 2026?
q.x: Deendayal (Kandla) led the major ports; Krishnapatnam led the non-major ports.

q.s: The Supreme Court has held that access to digital services forms part of the right guaranteed under:
q.x: Reading Article 21 as a right to live with dignity, the Court held that digital access is part of it.

q.s: The Export Preparedness Index is prepared by NITI Aayog in partnership with the:
q.x: NITI Aayog and the Institute for Competitiveness have published it since 2020; Maharashtra topped EPI 2024.

q.s: In the LEADS 2024 logistics ranking, Andhra Pradesh was placed in the category of:
q.x: AP was a 'Fast Mover' in LEADS 2024.

q.s: As per SRS 2024, the working-age group (15-59 years) forms about what share of India's population?
q.x: About 66.4%; those aged 60 and above form 9.7% and the 0-14 group about 24%.

q.s: The rural sex ratio in India is generally higher than the urban sex ratio mainly because of:
o: Male-selective migration from villages to towns
q.x: Men migrate to towns, lowering the urban ratio and raising the rural one.

q.s: As per SRS data, the Total Fertility Rate (TFR) of Andhra Pradesh is:
q.x: AP's TFR is 1.5 against India's 1.9; its child sex ratio is 944.

q.s: According to Census 2011, the largest category of main workers in Andhra Pradesh was:
q.x: Agricultural labourers formed about 44.6%, almost three times the cultivators.

q.s: Which of the following is a major cause of sea-level rise due to global warming?
q.x: Thermal expansion of warming water and melting of ice cause sea-level rise.

q.s: The Chips to Start-up (C2S) programme of the Government of India is implemented by:
q.x: C-DAC implements C2S (2022), which aims to train 85,000 students in five years.

q.s: The National Green Hydrogen Mission targets green hydrogen production by 2030 of:
q.x: 5 MMT a year, with 60-100 GW of electrolysers and about 6 lakh jobs.

q.s: The hybridoma technique for producing monoclonal antibodies was developed in 1975 by:
q.x: Georges Kohler and Cesar Milstein; it fuses an antibody-making B cell with a myeloma cell.

q.s: In the hybridoma technique, a myeloma cell is fused with a:
q.x: An antibody-making B cell is fused with a myeloma cell.

q.s: Gold nanoparticles appear red, purple or blue instead of yellow because of:
q.x: Surface plasmon resonance changes their colour.

q.s: Under the Drone Rules, 2021, a 'nano' drone weighs:
q.x: Nano up to 250 g; micro 250 g-2 kg; small 2-25 kg; medium 25-150 kg; large above 150 kg.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the four thematic hubs of the National Quantum Mission?
q.x: The hubs are quantum computing, communication, sensing and metrology, and materials and devices.

q.s: Wi-Fi 6 corresponds to which IEEE standard?
q.x: Wi-Fi 6 is 802.11ax; Wi-Fi 7 is 802.11be and WiMAX is 802.16.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the early Indian space programme is correct?
o: INCOSPAR was set up in 1962 under the Department of Space.
The Department of Space was set up in 1962.
INCOSPAR functioned under the Department of Atomic Energy.
q.x: INCOSPAR (1962) was under the DAE; ISRO came in 1969 and the DoS and Space Commission in 1972.

q.s: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was set up on:
q.x: ISRO was set up on 15 August 1969, superseding INCOSPAR.

q.s: The commercial arm of ISRO is:
q.x: NSIL is the commercial arm; IN-SPACe (2020, Ahmedabad) is the single-window regulator and promoter.

q.s: The NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) satellite was launched by:
q.x: NISAR went up on GSLV-F16 (2025).

q.s: All of India's navigation satellites launched since 2013 have been launched from:
q.x: All 11 went up from Sriharikota.

q.s: Which of the following satellite navigation systems is regional, NOT global?
q.x: NavIC (India) and QZSS (Japan) are regional; GPS, GLONASS, BeiDou and Galileo are global.

q.s: A GPS receiver needs signals from at least how many satellites to fix its position accurately?
q.x: Three for trilateration and a fourth to correct the receiver's clock error.

q.s: GAGAN, developed by ISRO and the Airports Authority of India, is a:
q.x: GAGAN is a satellite-based augmentation system for GPS; the IRNSS constellation is NavIC.

q.s: Kalpana-1, India's first exclusive weather satellite, was launched in 2002 by the:
q.x: PSLV launched Kalpana-1 (originally METSAT).

q.s: The heaviest payload launched by an Indian rocket, BlueBird Block-2, was launched by:
q.x: LVM3-M6 launched the roughly 6,100 kg BlueBird Block-2.

q.s: Aditya-L1, India's solar mission, was launched in September 2023 by:
q.x: PSLV-C57; LVM3-M4 launched Chandrayaan-3.

q.s: Bhargavastra, an Indian counter-drone system, neutralises drone swarms using:
q.x: Bhargavastra fires 64 micro-rockets; DRDO's D4 uses radar, jamming and laser kill.

q.s: Prithvi-I and Prithvi-II missiles use:
q.x: Prithvi-I and II are liquid-fuelled; Prithvi-II was inducted in 2003.

q.s: Digital Seva Setu, delivering government services to gram panchayats, is an initiative of:
q.x: It is a Gujarat initiative.

q.s: DigiLocker was launched in:
q.x: DigiLocker came in February 2015; UPI in 2016 and UMANG in 2017.

q.s: Which of the following statements about digital initiatives is correct?
o: UPI was launched in 2016 and UMANG in 2017.
q.x: UPI (2016) preceded UMANG (2017); PM eVIDYA and PM-WANI came in 2020 and DigiLocker in 2015.

q.s: Sharing genuine information, such as leaked private data, with the intent to cause harm is called:
q.x: Malinformation; disinformation is deliberately false content and misinformation is false content without intent to deceive.

q.s: India's peak electricity demand crossed which level in April 2026?
q.x: It rose from 183 GW (December 2020) to over 250 GW in April 2026.

q.s: India's Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 was adopted in:
q.x: Adopted in 2000, it favours competition and seeks self-reliance through domestic output and equity oil abroad.

q.s: Which of the following sources of energy is NOT derived from the Sun?
q.x: Tidal energy comes from the gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun, not solar radiation.

q.s: India's first commercial production of coal bed methane came from:
q.x: Raniganj; CBM is released by pumping water out of coal seams.

q.s: In the State Energy Efficiency Index (SEEI), States are classified into how many categories?
q.x: Four categories; AP was a Front Runner in the first index (2018).

q.s: The Nathpa Jhakri hydroelectric project is located in:
q.x: Nathpa Jhakri (1,500 MW) is on the Sutlej in Himachal Pradesh.

q.s: Which of the following hydroelectric projects is NOT in Himachal Pradesh?
q.x: Koyna is in Maharashtra.

q.s: Agenda 21 was adopted at the Earth Summit held in 1992 at:
q.x: Rio de Janeiro (1992); the first World Climate Conference was in 1979.

q.s: Wind power complements solar power in India because winds are strong:
o: In the evenings and during the south-west monsoon
q.x: Wind peaks in the evenings and in June-October, when solar output is low.

q.s: The State nodal agency for renewable energy in Andhra Pradesh is:
q.x: NREDCAP; APSECM handles energy conservation.

q.s: Which State leads India in installed solar power capacity?
q.x: Rajasthan leads in solar; Gujarat leads in total RE and wind.

q.s: The relationship between the cattle egret and grazing cattle is an example of:
q.x: Commensalism (+/0); the fig and fig wasp are mutualists and Penicillium shows amensalism.

q.s: The inhibition of other microbes by Penicillium is an example of:
q.x: Amensalism (-/0) through antibiosis.

q.s: Under the Indian Forest Act, 1927, reserved forests are dealt with in:
q.x: Chapter II covers reserved forests; village forests (Section 28) are reserved forests assigned to a village community.

q.s: Open burning of tyres, plastics and e-waste releases highly toxic compounds known as:
q.x: Dioxins and furans; in January 2026 the APPCB advised against open Bhogi burning.

q.s: The principle of 'absolute liability' was laid down by the Supreme Court in the:
o: Oleum gas leak case (M.C. Mehta v. Union of India)
q.x: The Oleum gas leak case (Shriram plant, Delhi) laid down absolute liability; Kamal Nath applied the public trust doctrine.

q.s: The 'public trust doctrine' was applied by the Supreme Court in:
o: Rural Litigation and Entitlement Kendra case
q.x: M.C. Mehta v. Kamal Nath (1997).

q.s: The Central Pollution Control Board was set up in 1974 under the:
o: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act
q.x: The Water Act, 1974, India's first pollution-control law, created the CPCB; the Air Act (1981) added noise in 1987.

q.s: Which of the following statements about pollution laws is correct?
o: The CPCB was set up under the Air Act, 1981.
The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974 is India's first pollution-control law.
Noise was added to the Water Act in 1987.
The Environment (Protection) Act was enacted in 1974.
q.x: The Water Act, 1974 came first and created the CPCB; noise was added to the Air Act in 1987; the EPA dates from 1986.

q.s: According to the IPBES Global Assessment (2019), how many species are threatened with extinction?
q.x: Up to 1 million species; about 40% of amphibians are threatened.

q.s: Which of the following statements about cyclones over the Indian seas is correct?
o: Cyclones are more frequent in the Bay of Bengal than in the Arabian Sea.
Cyclones are more frequent in the Arabian Sea than in the Bay of Bengal.
q.x: The Bay of Bengal sees more cyclones; Arabian Sea cyclones rose about 52% in 2001-2019 and marine heatwaves strengthen cyclones.

q.s: Ocean acidification is often called the:
q.x: It is called the 'evil twin of global warming'; the oceans absorb about a third of human CO2 and stay alkaline.

q.s: Which of the following statements about ocean acidification is NOT correct?
o: The oceans absorb about one-third of human CO2 emissions.
It is called the 'evil twin of global warming'.
The surface ocean is still alkaline.
It raises the concentration of carbonate ions in sea water.
q.x: Extra hydrogen ions bind carbonate ions, so carbonate concentration falls.

q.s: A marine heatwave is defined as sea-surface temperature 3-4 degrees C above average for at least:
q.x: At least five days; their number has doubled since 1982.

q.s: The Global Stocktake under the Paris Agreement is held every five years under:
q.x: Article 14; Article 13 is the Enhanced Transparency Framework and Article 28 deals with withdrawal.

q.s: As per the Economic Survey 2025-26, India's life expectancy in 2023 was:
q.x: 70.3 years, up from about 32 years at Independence.

q.s: The Integrated Disease Surveillance Programme (IDSP) is run by the:
q.x: NCDC runs IDSP and the Public Health Emergency Operations Centre; DGHS is MoHFW's technical arm.

q.s: Which of the following statements about epidemic laws is correct?
o: The Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897 clearly defines a 'dangerous epidemic disease'.
The 2020 amendment to the Epidemic Diseases Act was first issued as an ordinance in April 2020.
The draft Public Health Bill, 2017 was enacted in 2018.
The Epidemic Diseases Act was repealed in 2020.
q.x: The ordinance came in April 2020 and the Act in September 2020; the 1897 Act does not define the term and the 2017 Bill was never enacted.

q.s: In peritoneal dialysis, the filter used is the:
q.x: The peritoneum acts as the filter; dialysis cannot reabsorb nutrients the way kidney tubules do.

q.s: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was the project director of SLV-3, which placed which satellite in orbit in 1980?
q.x: SLV-3 put Rohini in orbit in 1980; Kalam later headed the IGMDP (1983).

q.s: Pokhran-II (1998) was led by A.P.J. Abdul Kalam along with:
q.x: R. Chidambaram; Raja Ramanna led Pokhran-I (1974).

q.s: The nodal ministry for the PM E-DRIVE scheme is the:
o: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
q.x: Ministry of Heavy Industries; outlay Rs 10,900 crore.

q.s: Among Indian exports, the sector with the highest share going to the US, hit by the 2025 tariff increase, was:
q.x: Carpets (58.6% US share) saw tariffs rise from 2.9% to 52.9%.

q.s: The largest component of India's foreign exchange reserves is:
q.x: FCA is the largest; the others are gold, SDRs and the Reserve Tranche Position.

q.s: Under India's 'managed float' exchange rate regime, the RBI intervenes in the forex market to:
o: Curb excessive volatility without targeting a level
Peg the rupee to a basket of gold
q.x: A managed float curbs volatility but does not target a level.

q.s: The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) was founded on:
q.x: ICAR was founded on 16 July 1929 (as the Imperial Council).

q.s: The Ministry of AYUSH, formed on 9 November 2014, grew out of a department under the:
o: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
q.x: It came from the Department of AYUSH under MoHFW.

q.s: The 153rd Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (2026) was held at:
q.x: Arusha, Tanzania; the Indian delegation was led by Harivansh.

q.s: The Secretariat of BIMSTEC is located at:
q.x: Dhaka; BIMSTEC was set up by the Bangkok Declaration of 6 June 1997.

q.s: Which of the following countries is NOT a member of BIMSTEC?
q.x: The seven members are Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Myanmar and Thailand.

q.s: India's research station Maitri in Antarctica was set up in:
q.x: Maitri 1989; Bharati 2012; Dakshin Gangotri (1983-84) is no longer operational.

q.s: The National Centre for Polar and Ocean Research (NCPOR), Goa, functions under the:
q.x: NCPOR (1998) is under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

q.s: Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) are a feature of the:
q.x: NDCs belong to the Paris Agreement; India is one of the 14 priority countries of Germany's IKI.

q.s: In 2025 the Sacred Relics of Lord Buddha were exhibited at Elista, the capital of which Russian republic?
q.x: Kalmykia, the only European territory where Buddhism is the main religion.

q.s: The motto of the New Delhi Declaration of the India-AI Impact Summit 2026 is:
q.x: 'Sarvajan Hitaya, Sarvajan Sukhaya'; the declaration is voluntary and non-binding.

q.s: The 16th India-Japan Annual Summit (July 2026) was held at:
q.x: New Delhi, with Japanese PM Sanae Takaichi.

q.s: Gilbert F. Houngbo, Director-General of the International Labour Organization, is from:
q.x: Togo; Tedros is Ethiopian and Okonjo-Iweala Nigerian.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of head of organisation and nationality is NOT correct?
q.x: Houngbo is from Togo.

q.s: 2026 has been designated as the ASEAN-India Year of:
